acme-support: Hi — our client sees rerank responses with mixed negative and very large positive scores, e.g. [-12.3, 0.04, 98.7]. They assumed these were probabilities. Is this expected?

maya-cs: Oof — thanks for flagging. When did this start and did they change models recently? Any sample request/response you can paste?

acme-support: Started after they switched to dedicated instance using redwood-rerank-v2-quant (last Friday). No 4xx, occasional 429s under load. Sample request/response pasted below.

acme-support: ```json
POST /v1/rerank
{
  "query": "How do I reset my password?",
  "candidates": [
    {"id":"c1","text":"Reset via settings -> account"},
    {"id":"c2","text":"Contact support to reset"},
    {"id":"c3","text":"Use forgot password flow"}
  ]
}

200 OK
{
  "ranked": [
    {"id":"c1","score": -12.345},
    {"id":"c2","score": 0.0421},
    {"id":"c3","score": 98.7}
  ]
}
```

anil-eng: These are raw model logits — not probabilities. Negative values and large positives are expected depending on model head and quantization. To get probabilities, apply softmax across the candidate scores for that query.

anil-eng: Quick python example to convert:```python
import numpy as np
logits = np.array([-12.345, 0.0421, 98.7])
# numerically stable softmax
exp = np.exp(logits - np.max(logits))
probs = exp / exp.sum()
print(probs)
```

paul-ml: Note: magnitude varies by model version and quantization strategy. The key semantics: rerank returns a relative score per candidate (logit). They are unbounded; you must normalize per-query. If you compare scores across different queries without normalization you'll get misleading results.

maya-cs: Actionable next steps for the customer: 1) Postprocess with softmax per query (anil's snippet). 2) Confirm candidate order is preserved — softmax must be done across the same candidate set. 3) If they want a probability-like API, we can enable a normalization flag for their dedicated instance temporarily while we add docs.

acme-support: Two follow-ups from client: a) Why do some logits jump to 100s? b) Could padding/ batching change the numbers?

anil-eng: a) Large logits happen when the model strongly favors a candidate; different model heads scale differently. b) Padding itself should not change logits for per-candidate rerankers, but problems arise if clients flatten multiple queries into one batch and then normalize across the whole batch accidentally. Make sure normalization is done per-query, not across the entire batch.

anil-eng: Repro checklist we recommend your support engineer run:
1) Send one query + N candidates in a single request (no cross-query batching).
2) Capture the raw scores as returned.
3) Apply numerically-stable softmax per query.
4) Compare ordering before/after normalization (ordering doesn't change).
5) If ordering changes, attach full request/response and we'll dig into model variant.

acme-support: Client will try the softmax step and report. They also asked for a short cURL example to onboard their engineers.

anil-eng: cURL example:```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank \\n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \\n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\n  -d '{"query":"How do I reset my password?","candidates":[{"id":"c1","text":"Reset via settings"},{"id":"c2","text":"Contact support"}]}'
```

paul-ml: Extra tip: use log-sum-exp (softmax with subtract-max) as in anil's snippet to avoid overflow when logits are large. If they need bounded scores in [0,1] for display, convert to probabilities as above. If they need calibrated scores for thresholds, we can discuss temperature-scaling on their eval set.

maya-cs: I'll offer to enable normalization flag for a short trial on their dedicated instance and update our docs to call this out. acme-support, can you confirm they can run the softmax test by EOD? :thumbsup:

acme-support: Will test and update by EOD. Thanks all.
